Lisa Sabatino to receive 2026 Stan Schaeffer Education Community Leadership Award
Lisa Sabatino will be honored with the Stan Schaeffer Education Community Leadership Award by C3 this December for her decades-long service as lead nurse at Collinsville schools. Colleagues cite her leadership during health crises while local data highlights broad engagement across diverse student populations.
Lisa Sabatino, lead school nurse for Collinsville Community Unit School District 10, was selected to receive the 2026 Stan Schaeffer Education Community Leadership Award, according to an Oct. 15 announcement by the Collinsville Community Collaboration (C3).
C3 is a partnership between the City of Collinsville, the Collinsville Chamber of Commerce and Collinsville Community Unit School District 10. The organization recognizes excellence in community and public service. Since 2018, C3 has held annual awards honoring organizations and individuals for outstanding contributions to the community. This year’s awards dinner will take place on Wednesday, December 2 at the Gateway Center in Collinsville.
The Stan Schaeffer Education Community Leadership Award honors the late Stan Schaeffer, a retired educator and former mayor of Collinsville. The award is given to a district employee who has made significant contributions in education that positively impact the greater Collinsville community. Recipients must be leaders and role models within CUSD 10 who work to further education and create positive change.
Sabatino holds bachelor’s and master’s degrees in nursing from Southern Illinois University Edwardsville. She began her career as a registered nurse providing pre- and post-op surgical care before becoming a certified school nurse for CUSD 10 in August 1997. She currently serves as both lead nurse for the district and school nurse at John Renfro Elementary School.
Director of Special Education Alison Underwood nominated Sabatino for this award. “Nurse Lisa is the standard of excellence in school health leadership. She’s an extraordinary leader who doesn’t just keep our district compliant, but elevates our entire school community,” according to Underwood. “From navigating complex state mandates to mentoring her nursing team with grace, she acts as an unwavering advocate for every student and an innovative, trusted resource for our staff and families.”
Sabatino has also served as a CPR instructor for over three decades, initiated programs such as Automated External Defibrillator implementation across schools—resulting in successful emergency responses—and developed outreach efforts like CPR certification classes open to parents and students fourth grade or older.
“My passion for school nursing lies in educating students and staff, and finding resources for families,” she says.
Superintendent Dr. Mark B. Skertich said, “Nurse Lisa is a consummate professional who takes great pride in making sure our students receive the best possible care every day... Her commitment to student health, staff development, and the well-being of every child makes her an invaluable member of our Kahok Family.”
Collinsville Community Unit School District 10 represents Madison and St. Clair counties; it enrolled more than six thousand students during recent years across multiple elementary schools through high school levels; its teacher workforce numbers over four hundred with average salaries exceeding sixty thousand dollars per year; most teachers are women; chronic truancy rates are below statewide averages; per-student spending was $16,872 during one recent academic year—all according to the Illinois State Board of Education.
Sabatino plans to retire at the end of the 2026-27 school year after thirty years as a school nurse but intends to continue serving her community through teaching CPR courses.
